description.from:
As an editor, I want each Story to state its language and each translation to be its own Story joined to the original by a language group, so versions, approvals and published pages stay separate per language without special cases.

Design: localization = sibling lineage (option B in the plan). Item and PublishedItem gain language (BCP 47, required) and languageGroupId (tenant-prefixed); localization versions record sourceLineageId, sourceVersionNumber, sourceContentHash. One new GSI languageGroupId+language per table per deploy (Item first, PublishedItem next). Every existing row gets language set explicitly by a bounded, resumable backfill before code reads it: no 'missing means primary' default. Group facts (section, concepts, references, stars, Cyclotron prediction) are read from the primary, never copied. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450).

Feature: Language groups

Scenario: A Story's first translation forms its language group
  Given an English Story with no translations
  When an editor creates its Spanish localization
  Then the English Story's language group is its own lineage
  And the Spanish localization belongs to that group with language es

Scenario: Approving one language never approves another
  Given an approved English version and an unreviewed Spanish localization in the same group
  When an editor tries to publish the Spanish localization
  Then publishing is refused until the Spanish version itself is approved

Scenario: Finding a Story's languages reads only that Story's group
  Given a site with many Stories
  When the newsroom lists the languages of one Story
  Then it queries that Story's language group only
description.to:
As an editor, I want each Story to state its language and each translation to be its own Story joined to the original by a language group, so versions, listings, approvals and published pages stay separate per language without special cases.

Design (option B): Item and PublishedItem gain language (required) and languageGroupId (tenant-prefixed); localization versions record sourceLineageId, sourceVersionNumber, sourceContentHash. One GSI languageGroupId+language per table per deploy. Found in the publish-path review (PPY-d50d27): typeStatus, sectionStatus and headStageKey carry the language for every row so English listings never include translations; localization ids are {primaryLineageId}--{languageTag}, not item_id_for(section, slug), so a shared slug cannot collide and JIT creation is idempotent; every itemBySlug call site filters by language. One bounded backfill writes language and the listing-key language on every existing row first; no 'missing means primary' default. Group facts are read from the primary. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450), revised 2026-11-12 with Ryan's decisions.

Feature: Language groups

Scenario: A Story's first translation forms its language group
  Given an English Story with no translations
  When its Spanish localization is generated
  Then the Spanish localization belongs to the English Story's group with language es

Scenario: English listings never show translations
  Given an English article with a published Spanish localization
  When the English articles listing and feed are rendered
  Then only the English article appears

Scenario: A Chinese localization sharing the English slug keeps its own record
  Given a Chinese localization that uses the English Story's slug
  When it is published
  Then the English record is unchanged and each is found by slug within its own language

Scenario: Generating the same localization twice
  Given a Spanish localization already exists for a Story
  When generation runs again for that Story in Spanish
  Then it adds a version to the same localization rather than creating another
